basis: Cerebellar, spinal cord and peripheral nervous system degeneration; other organ disease is subtype-specific.
Hydrocephalus and intellectual disability define the syndrome; scoliosis occurs in 30-79%. Hearing and optic nerve abnormalities occur in fewer than 30%.
Syndromic intellectual disability; short stature, facial dysmorphism and mild clinodactyly do not establish substantial skeletal damage.
Benign adipose neoplasm arising in the rectum.
Developmental eye disease with brain abnormalities; developmental delay in 20/20. Quantified digit, hearing and endocrine abnormalities are below 30%.
Immune-mediated giant-cell inflammation directly damages myocardium, causing arrhythmias and heart failure.
Tumour originates in the ovary; resemblance to renal Wilms tumour does not establish kidney involvement. Reproductive organs have no axis.
Inherited isoleucine degradation defect, usually asymptomatic. Neurologic and muscular findings in selected symptomatic cases do not establish a 30% prevalence.
SOD1-related motor neuron degeneration; muscle atrophy, dysphagia and respiratory weakness result from denervation rather than separate direct organ disease.
Inherited cerebral small-vessel disorders produce destructive brain cavities and neurologic dysfunction; extracerebral findings vary by subtype.
Scaly inflammatory disease of scalp and facial skin; no specific infectious or immune-mediated mechanism is established for this umbrella.
Carcinoma originates in lacrimal gland epithelium; the lacrimal system belongs to the ocular axis.
Carcinoma originates in the male breast, which has no axis; distant spread is not a defining organ involvement.
Loss of urinary continence is lower urinary tract dysfunction; pelvic floor weakness is an underlying cause rather than damage caused by incontinence.
Psychiatric disorder defined by intentional symptom production; no consistent directly damaged organ is intrinsic to the diagnosis.
Mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation defect; cardiomyopathy in 4/4 and ptosis/external ophthalmoplegia in 2/4. Renal, hepatic and hearing findings each occur in 1/4.
Hypogonadotropic hypogonadism defines the disease; persistent loss of smell occurs in 30-79%. Hearing loss and clefts lack qualifying frequency evidence.
GPI-anchor biosynthesis defect with developmental delay in 12/12 and cerebellar atrophy in 10/12; hypotonia does not independently establish muscle disease.
Malignant neoplasm of the glans penis, a reproductive site outside the axes; urethral involvement is not established.
Hamartomatous polyp arises in the stomach.
Umbrella for inherited or acquired biotin deficiency; skin and neurologic damage vary with cause and severity, without established prevalence across the group.
Benign adipose neoplasm originates in the pleura; possible chest wall extension does not establish common musculoskeletal damage.
Vertebral dysplasia and microtia in 3/3; anal atresia and ASD each 2/3. Skin aplasia 2/3 and neurologic/urinary abnormalities 1/3 omitted under four-axis cap.
Benign urothelial epithelial neoplasm of the urethra.
Lysosomal storage disease with skeletal dysplasia; developmental delay/intellectual disability in most per definition and visual impairment 80-99%. Cardiac data reflect one case.
